what_happened: Scene layout 5 / style 5: single-basin dark sink, gooseneck faucet; romaine lettuce (Lettuce009) in a perforated colander (Colander008) on the counter right of the sink, next to a mesh utensil holder. Stage 0 fast: fingers on the lever 112-178 (close at 118), water on at 170. Stage 1: the arm reached the colander 260-400 (wrist: colander rim and handle with the lettuce), closed at 404-410 at the rim (close_event 406 touching the lettuce, width 0.003 = fully closed, nothing lifted). The colander stayed behind: from 420 the wrist view shows only the empty basin and the stream (colander handle leaving the bottom of the view at 420-428), yet the arm carried on to the stream and moved around it empty-handed 424-540 (another close on nothing at 464, opened at ~512). 556-1100 it returned to the colander, which had been dragged ~10 cm toward the sink's right rim, and hovered/pushed at it with open fingers (width 0.08 from 520 to the end) without closing again. washed_time 0.
causal_chain: water on 170 (fast) -> fingers closed at the colander rim at ~406 but slipped off, colander not lifted -> empty 'carry' to the stream 424-540 -> back at the colander 556-1100 with open fingers, never re-grasped (~540 steps) -> timeout
self_recovery: It went back to the colander after the empty carry (556) and nudged it toward the sink, but never closed the fingers again; failed.
official_criterion_notes: close_event 406 lists 'touching lettuce' while the fingers were really at the colander rim; the lettuce is the only tracked object.

packet_facts: close_events 118 (lever), 406 (0.003, touching lettuce, not lifted), 464 (0.002, nothing)

uncertain_about: The agent view shows a greenish patch at the gripper 416-468 that could be a lettuce leaf edge caught between the fingers, but the wrist view at the stream shows nothing held and the colander stays on the counter, so I read it as an empty carry. When exactly the colander was dragged toward the sink rim (406-416 or 556-600) is unclear. Colander008 pattern: all three slipped colander grasps in this task are on this colander model (s6, s14, s19); no visible difference from successful Colander008 grasps at the moment of closing.
